title: Robo Arm
description: A robotic camera arm runs a programmed path with inhuman precision, repeatable every take for product geometry or a stunt match. No operator shake; the spline is the performance.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: The path must be identical every take. Commercials, previs stages, a bottle that must match a CGI pass, a stunt that must fit a plate: the arm does not interpret.
A human dolly will drift. An orbit-360 can be walked and will breathe.
Bolt cam is a throw, not a repeatable spline (unless the throw is itself robotic). If you want error and life, do not use the arm.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Motion-control arm or a six-axis robot, programmed XYZ and pan/tilt/roll. Speed can be inhumanly even or inhumanly fast.
Product tables, crash pads, or a repeatable orbit. Prompt: Robotic arm move around [Subject], programmed path, inhuman precision, product or stunt geometry.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it when takes must match: VFX, product, a stunt plate. Do not use it for a scene that needs human drift.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a steadicam orbit. The tell: a little sway, a human accel.
The fix: write programmed path, identical takes, no operator shake.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Robo Arm in film?
A robo arm is a robotic camera on a programmed path, repeatable every take, with no human shake. Product and stunt geometry live here.
Robo Arm vs 360-Degree Orbit
An orbit-360 is a circular walk or dolly and can breathe. A robo arm can orbit, but the point is a programmed spline that matches take to take.
When should I use Robo Arm?
Use it when the path must be identical: VFX plates, product, stunts. Do not use it when you want human error.
How do I prompt Robo Arm for AI image or video?
Write a programmed path with no shake. Example: Robotic arm move around [Subject], programmed path, inhuman precision, product or stunt geometry.
